claims.text: HEA multilayers can be used to produce a transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep.
Systematically varying interface coherency can cause a transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep mechanisms.
The relevant initial material is an HEA multilayer with variable interface coherency.
The proposed intervention is systematic variation of interface coherency.
The proposed transition applies under high-temperature and high-stress conditions.
Grain-boundary sliding and dislocation movement are the structural mediators of the creep response.
Interface coherency affects creep behavior through its effects on grain-boundary sliding and dislocation movement.
Diffusion-mediated creep is the baseline mechanism.
Dislocation-mediated creep is the boundary or alternative mechanism.
A controlled experiment can test the hypothesis by varying interface coherency and measuring creep rate, grain-boundary sliding, and dislocation movement.
Failure to observe a significant change in creep mechanism as interface coherency varies would falsify the hypothesis.
